sentences.text: Dollosuchoides is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodilian known colloquially as the Crocodile of Maransart.
The holotype specimen IRScNB 482 was discovered in 1915 and prepared between 1926 and 1927 by Hubert, Mehschaert, and Jean de Kleermaeker.
Louis Dollo intended to describe the holotype in 1931 but died before he could publish the description.
The specimen was originally referred to the genus Dollosuchus by Swinton in 1937 before being moved to its own genus by Brochu in 2007.
Dollosuchoides was traditionally classified as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae.
Recent molecular studies suggest that Tomistominae, including Dollosuchoides, belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
A 2018 study indicates Dollosuchoides is a basal gavialoid, predating the common ancestor of gharials and false gharials.
The parent group of Dollosuchoides is Gavialoidea.
The type species of the genus Dollosuchoides is Dollosuchoides densmorei.
Fossils of Dollosuchoides have been found in the Brussels Formation of Maransart, Belgium, dating to the Middle Eocene.
Dollosuchoides lived during the Lutetian stage, approximately 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
